+# Acceptance Criteria
+
+Rules:
+
+- Criteria lines use the exact format `- ACn: <criterion>`.
+- Every criterion ends with [verify: exec `<command>`],
+  [verify: invariant `<command>`], [verify: judged] or
+  [verify: none — <reason>].
+- After `flow freeze` this file is checksum-protected: any edit outside
+  `keryx flow ac update` fails every gate and status transition.
+- Completion requires every ACn to be confirmed via
+  `keryx flow ac confirm <id> <ACn>`.
+
+## Criteria
+
+- AC1: A SIGTERM or SIGINT delivered to `refreshLayers` in each phase after the lock is taken (recover, build, wiki, memory, `layers.json` write) leaves no `refresh.lock`, no detached worktree and no staging directory, and the process still exits by the signal. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/layers-signal.test.ts`]
+- AC2: When the wiki reader, the memory reader or `computeAffected` throws, `keryx review layers block --json` reports that source as `unavailable` with a reason, and the text block prints `<source>: unavailable (<reason>)`; a source with no relevant items still prints as empty, not as unavailable. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/layers-payload.test.ts`]
+- AC3: After a persistent graph-build failure, a second `ensurePackageLayers` at the same head inside the retry window creates no worktree and runs no build; `--force` or a new head runs the build again. [verify: exec `bun test src/commands/review-layers.test.ts`]
+- AC4: The timeout test in `src/tui/review-layers-child.test.ts` fails when the timeout kill is removed and when the child prints no JSON, and asserts the child process is gone. [verify: exec `bun test src/tui/review-layers-child.test.ts`]
+- AC5: The `/reviews` double-start guard has a test with two views over one dir (second start refused while the first is pending) and one with two dirs (both start), and the pending promise is settled in a `finally`. [verify: exec `bun test src/tui/reviews-inspector.test.ts`]
+- AC6: Tests named after round ids (`layers-round2.test.ts` and the `R2-nn` prefixes in it) are renamed after the behaviour they pin; no test count is lost. [verify: invariant `bun test src/review 2>&1 | tail -4`]
+- AC7: A mutation run with the focused command widened to the TUI and command-risk test files kills the mutants for AC1 to AC5 (a mutant per fix: signal handler removed, `unavailable` dropped, retry window removed, timeout kill removed, guard made per-view). [verify: judged]
+- AC8: `bun run check` passes and the CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` section names the fixes. [verify: exec `bun run check`]

A report without that block ingests as `findings: in=0`, and every `--verifications` claim naming one of its findings is then discarded as unresolvable — because the finding it names is not in the round.

+   `~/.local/bin/keryx` is an installed build, and its version lags the working tree. It is NOT the working tree. Every `keryx …` invocation — including `keryx review ingest`, which is how a managed review package is recorded — runs that build, so the review pipeline routinely does not exercise the code being reviewed.

+4. [1.787] Theme switch repaints already-rendered chrome via old-slot value matching (lesson/accepted) - lessons/theme-switch-repaint.md
+   `/theme` in the OpenTUI shell applied and persisted correctly on 0.2.66, but `applyTheme` (src/tui/shell-chrome.ts) only recolored the chrome's OWN surfaces (renderer background, sidebar border, docks, composer, `/`-menu). Every renderable painted EARLIER with `getTheme()` — transcript frames (user echoes, code-segment boxes, block bodies, side-worker boxes), tone-colored block headers (`theme.error`/`theme.tool`), dock/queue-dock buttons, sidebar panels — kept the old palette's hex in its `borderColor`/`backgroundColor`/`fg` props, so a dark→dark switch (groknight↔tokyonight) looked like "the theme did not apply". Fix: on every `applyTheme`, walk the renderable trees (transcript, docks, sidebarTop, menu, composer, header, footer) and rewrite any prop whose color equals an OLD theme slot hex to the NEW slot hex.

+# Review layers: reliability and test tails of PR 1006 round 3
+
+Status: draft, criteria awaiting operator approval before freeze
+Source: agent finding (origin: agent-finding)
+
+## Problem
+
+Round 3 of PR 1006 (flow 431) skipped seven findings that are not refactors: three reliability gaps in the layers refresh
+and four weak or misnamed tests. They shipped in 0.3.113 as known residuals.
+
+- R3-06: the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler lives only inside `withDetachedWorktree`. A signal after the graph build (wiki, memory,
+  `layers.json` write) kills the process without releasing `refresh.lock`, and a lock with a fresh mtime reads as held.
+- R3-12: `wikiFor`, `memoryFor` and `affectedFor` swallow reader failures, so a failure looks the same as "nothing relevant".
+- R3-29: a package whose graph build failed persistently is rebuilt on every `ensurePackageLayers` call (worktree, full
+  build, cleanup, behind `refresh.lock`).
+- R3-22, R3-23, R3-28, R3-31: a timeout test that cannot tell a timeout from a no-JSON exit, a double-start guard test that
+  cannot tell a module-level guard from a per-view one, a fixed 150 ms wait in `blockedWhile`, and test names that carry
+  round ids.
+
+## Expected Outcome
+
+A signal at any phase of a layers refresh leaves no `refresh.lock`, no detached worktree and no staging directory. A reader
+failure shows in the layers block as `unavailable` with a reason. A persistently failing build is not retried at the same
+head inside a short window unless `--force`. The four tests fail against the mutants they were meant to catch.
+
+## Outcome criteria
+
+- Источник: `.metaproject/flows/431-2026-10-12-metaproject-in-review/reviews/2026-10-14-pr-1006-round3-72920f1d` (skipped findings R3-06, 12, 22, 23, 28, 29, 31); operator choice A+B, helyx poll 168, 2026-10-14T04:44Z
+- Эффект (формализация агента): refresh не оставляет блокировку после сигнала; отказ ридера виден в блоке слоёв; повторная сборка того же головного коммита после сбоя не идёт при каждом вызове; четыре теста ловят то, ради чего написаны.
+- Как наблюдать (предложение агента): тест, который шлёт сигнал в фазе wiki и проверяет отсутствие `refresh.lock`; строка `wiki: unavailable (...)` в `keryx review layers block`; второй вызов `ensurePackageLayers` после сбоя не создаёт worktree; мутанты тестов убиваются.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+R3-08, 10, 11, 13..18, 27 (refactors and performance, later flow). R3-28 is optional: done only if it needs no production change.

 ## [Unreleased]
 
+### Fixed
+- **Tails of the layers refresh (flow 444).** A `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT` in any phase of `keryx review layers refresh` (the sweep after the lock, the graph build, the wiki refresh, the memory index) now releases the lock, removes the detached checkout and the staging directory, and re-raises the signal; before, only part of the phases cleaned up. A graph that failed at the same head is not rebuilt for 5 minutes after the failure (`graph.failedAt`, so repeated polling does not extend the window); `--force` or a new head rebuilds it at once. A reader that failed is reported under `unavailable` (section and reason) in the layers block, its text lines and the reviewer-input schema, instead of looking like an empty result: the wiki, the memory, unreadable wiki pages and the affected-files computation. A TUI refresh that hits its timeout says "did not finish within Ns and was stopped" instead of a parse error.
+- **Tests are named after behaviour.** `layers-round2.test.ts` became `layers-refresh-lifecycle.test.ts` and the `R2-nn` tags are gone from the layers tests. New tests cover the signal at every phase, the retry window, `unavailable`, the child timeout (the process is gone) and one refresh guard shared by every open view of a package.

 ## [0.3.113] - 2026-10-14
 
 ### Added
 - **Metaproject layers, a chunked pass and a coverage gate in managed reviews (flow 431).** `keryx review layers refresh|status|block` refreshes the graph (built at the PR head in a detached worktree in the OS temp directory, removed after the build; an intact graph of the same head is reused unless `--force`), the wiki (`wiki refresh`, a dry run unless `--write-wiki`) and the memory index for one review and writes `layers.json`, with no model call; `wiki enrich` stays the only model step and is never automatic. Reviewer payloads carry a bounded `layers` block, and each dispatch run records `layersUsed` counted from `<input-dir>/tool-calls/<reviewer>.jsonl` (`unknown`, never zero, without a log). `keryx review chunks plan|estimate|next|record|merge` reviews the blast-radius files the 40-file cap dropped, with an estimate and a 25x40 ceiling (`reviewChunks.maxPasses`); `keryx review coverage` counts in-scope, covered, omitted and uncovered files; `review complete` refuses while a file is uncovered unless `--waive-coverage "<quote>"` records the waiver. `/reviews` (sidebar, Review depth tab, `l` and `c` actions) and `/review layers` show the same lines. The reviewer skills share one instruction block for the layers; the skills were tightened to make room and five skill-length ceilings in `src/gdskills/skill-length-ceilings.ts` moved down. `saveRoutingConfig` now keeps the other top-level keys of `routing.config.json` (it wrote only the routing table before); its only callers are the `/routing` inspector and the set and unset helpers in the same module.
 ### Changed
 - **The round limit of a turn follows the permission mode.** A turn was capped at 40 model rounds in every mode, and the question "Increase limit and continue / Cancel" was the one prompt `auto` still left: a review shell sat on it for about 50 minutes. The default is now 40 in `ask` (unchanged), 200 in `trust` and 200 in `auto`; `KERYX_AGENT_MAX_ROUNDS` still wins in every mode and 200 stays the ceiling. In `auto` reaching the limit never asks: below 200 the turn extends itself and prints the `[budget]` line, and at 200 it stops with a `[budget]` message that names the ceiling. In `trust` and `ask` the question stays, and a yes grants one more allotment of the mode (200 or 40). The mode is read at the start of each turn, so `/mode` takes effect on the next turn; `/mode` (readline and TUI picker) and `/help` show the limit. Subagents, which is how review waves run, follow the same rule in `auto`: default 40 rounds, a `max_rounds` request honored up to 200; in `ask` and `trust` they keep 10 and 24.
 - **Automatic review is a run mode, not a permission mode.** Naming an automatic review in a request ("run an automatic review of PR 12", "автоматическое ревью") marks that one turn: it gets the 200-round limit with no question and the same `[budget]` stop as `auto`, whatever the permission mode. `keryx review start|attach|ingest --automatic` records `manifest.automatic: true`; `review status` prints the run mode. For the package the run created, the shell approves without asking the review's own commands: `start|attach|ingest --automatic`, `status` and `complete <review>`, `ledger build`, `severity-audit`, `context-collect`, `compare-reference` and `mutate` with `--package <review>`, `retry-plan --manifest`, `scope` and `blast-radius`, and `apply_patch` inside the package directory. Pipes, `;`, redirects, another review's id or path, every other subcommand and every hard floor (destructive, credentials, untrusted content, a hook's ask, publish lease, read-only) still ask. `ask_user` is answered with its recommended option and logged, except the two emergencies (`gate-waiver` and `reduced-reviewer-set`, accepted only after `review complete` has refused) and questions tagged irreversible or with a review `policy`, which go to the host (arbiter or operator). A count of manual and automatic inputs is written to `automatic-run-inputs.json` in the package. There is no way around the completion gate.
 
 ### Deferred majors of PR 940 and PR 975 (flow 441)
 
 - **F-001, a queued line that starts no turn no longer stalls the queue.** One `drainNext` helper (`src/tui/main-queue.ts`) owns "run the next queued line, and keep going while it started no turn"; a slash command run inline (`/compact`, `/model`, `/goal`, `/connect`) used to leave the lines behind it waiting for the operator. The three call sites keep their differences, and the drain is bounded by the queue length. The main turn loop's queue moved to `src/tui/turn-loop.ts` so the behaviour is tested headlessly. `onSettle()` now also fires after a drain that ran only non-turn slash lines and ended idle.
 - **F-007, `bun test` is routine only in the project root.** It needs an unchanged, preload-free `bunfig.toml` (hash recorded at turn start, fail closed without a baseline), a closed flag list (`--bail`, `--only`, `--todo`, `--rerun-each N`, `--timeout N`), and no untrusted content earlier in the turn. This repository's own `bunfig.toml` carries a `preload`, so `bun test` never auto-runs here.
 - **F-008, routine review commands cannot write outside the project.** `keryx review slice --out`, `retry-plan --manifest|--state` and `dispatch-check --manifest` refuse a path outside the project root and `.metaproject/` (symlink-safe), by one rule shared by the commands and the trust table. `dispatch-check --manifest -` reads the manifest from standard input; `-` there is not a file name.
 - **D-01, `parseReviewResult` returns the reviewer's result.** It reads a bare JSON reply and the object after a `REVIEW_RESULT` marker (a marker counts only at the start of a line and outside a fenced block), and fails closed on a truncated or ambiguous reply (a fenced sample plus a bare object with a different status gives no result and the reviewer is re-dispatched). **Behaviour change:** a status-only retry reply saved as `raw/<reviewer>.txt` now makes `ledger build` report NOT READY ("no parseable REVIEW_RESULT block") instead of being ignored.
 - **D-02, flow acceptance criteria that name a missing test file now fail a test.** `src/flow/verify-exec-files.test.ts` checks every `[verify: exec ...]` line.
 - **Replay of closed review rounds.** `src/review/replay.ts` replays every tracked `raw/` reviewer reply under `.metaproject/flows` through the old and the new result parser; the report is checked in under the flow and every difference carries a recorded decision.
 - **Shell-syntax hardening of the routine-command gate (F-045).** A glued `--flag=--option` spelling, a review flag whose value starts with `-`, and any argument the shell would build differently than the gate judged (unquoted `$`, backslash, braces, `*`, `?`, `[` or a word-initial `~`) now ask for approval. Every git call that takes a typed revision refuses a leading `-` (`assertGitRevision`) and puts `--end-of-options` before it. **Quote such arguments to stay auto-approved:** `git show 'HEAD@{1}'`, `keryx ctx rg foo '\.ts'`. `--end-of-options` needs **git 2.24 or newer**.

   (`toBe(3)` → `toBeDefined()`) is invisible, and is stated as invisible rather

 - **Suppression added.** `eslint-disable`, `@ts-expect-error`, `@ts-ignore`,
   `# type: ignore`, `# noqa`, `//nolint`, `@SuppressWarnings`, `#[allow(` and
   the rest — on an added line, after a comment opener, with no quote before it.
   A marker listed in a string array is not a suppression, a suppression being
   *deleted* is not a finding, and a suppression that merely **moved** — removed
   and re-added byte-identical inside the same region — is not "added". That
   forgiveness is counted: each removal pays for exactly one identical addition,
   so a region that deletes one marker and adds three reports two.
 
 It sees only what the pre-filter retained, so a threshold lowered inside a
 vendored or generated path is invisible by construction — and it depends on
 `review scope` never dropping a comment that carries a tool directive, which is
 why that carve-out exists.
 
 ### `review layers`, `review chunks` and `review coverage`
 
-A review reads three derived layers besides the diff: the code graph, the wiki and the memory. `keryx review layers refresh --package <dir>` brings them up to date and writes `<dir>/layers.json`; a managed review start, attach or ingest does it for you, and so does any `dispatch-check` or `blast-radius` given `--package`. **It calls no model.** It runs the graph build, `wiki refresh` and `memory index` (without `--embeddings`); `wiki enrich` is the only model step in the wiki and is never run automatically. The wiki refresh is a dry run unless you pass `--write-wiki`. A graph that is intact at the same head is reused and `--force` rebuilds it. One refresh runs per package at a time, and a second one waits for the first for up to 16 minutes.

The wiki refresh is a dry run unless you pass `--write-wiki`. A graph that is intact at the same head is reused and `--force` rebuilds it. A graph that failed at the same head is not rebuilt for 5 minutes (counted from the failure, so polling does not extend it); `--force` or a new head rebuilds it at once. A reader that failed (the wiki, the memory, or the affected-files computation) is reported under `unavailable` in the layers block with its reason, not as an empty result. A `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT` during any phase releases the lock and removes the checkout and the staging directory. One refresh runs per package at a time, and a second one waits for the first for up to 16 minutes.
 
 - The graph is built at the PR head into `<dir>/layers/graph`, in a fresh worktree; the tracked graph artifacts, the working tree and the PR are not touched. `layers.json` records the commit it was built from, and `graph@<sha7> = head` means it equals the PR head.
 - The wiki and the memory are read from the project's working copy. `layers.json` marks how far that copy is from the PR head (`differs`, with the commits and wiki/memory paths between).
 - `layers status` prints the same lines plus the coverage counts. `layers block --files a,b` prints the bounded, deterministic `layers` block a reviewer payload carries for those files: affected files, symbol neighbours, related tests, wiki pages and memory entries, with a command that fetches whatever was cut.
 - Per reviewer run the package records `layersUsed` (`graph`, `wiki`, `memory`, `ctx`), counted from the reviewer's tool-call log, `<input-dir>/tool-calls/<reviewer>.jsonl`, one JSON line per call. A run without a log is `unknown`, never zero, and never blocks `ledger build`, `compare-reference` or `review complete`.
 
 The blast radius keeps at most 40 files per pass; the rest are `dropped`. `review chunks plan` writes `<dir>/chunks.json`, a deterministic split of every dropped file into chunks (at most 40 files and the slice byte cap), each file in exactly one chunk; no dropped files means no plan. Chunks run one at a time through `review-regression` on the middle tier: `chunks next` prints the chunk to dispatch, `chunks record` takes what it returned and applies the retry plan (a failed chunk is retried per the plan, else stays `pending`), and `chunks merge` writes `<dir>/chunk-pass.json` with the state of each chunk and the merged findings (two on the same file and line count once).
 
 `chunks estimate` states the chunk count, the files, the estimated tokens and cost at the middle tier, and the duration before a run. The ceiling is **25 passes of 40 files (1,000 files)**; `reviewChunks.maxPasses` in `routing.config.json` moves it. In automatic mode a run at or under the ceiling goes through without a question and a run over it asks once; in interactive mode a run over it waits for `--answer yes --quote "<words>"`. The estimate and the answer are recorded in `<dir>/chunk-estimate.json`.
 
 `review coverage` writes `<dir>/coverage.json` and prints four counts for the changed files and the blast radius together: in scope, covered, covered by a named omission (with the reasons), and uncovered. Every changed file lands in a slice or under a named omission, and `coverage.json` lists each omitted file with its reason. **`review complete` refuses while any in-scope file is uncovered**: it names the count, the first files and the command that runs the missing chunks. The only way past is `--waive-coverage "<operator quote>"`, which records the quote, the time and the files not reviewed in the dispatch record and shows the waiver in the report and the panel. The waiver needs an interactive terminal (a command run from a script or an agent is refused), its quote must be at least 8 characters with a letter or digit once the flag text is removed, and the command asks for confirmation in every permission mode. There is no "unchecked remainder" outcome.
 
 In the shell, `/reviews` shows one line per review (`graph@<sha7> = head|differs`, wiki and memory divergence, `layers used n/m`, `unknown k`, `chunks d/t, uncovered u`) in the sidebar and the full lines in the Review depth tab, with `l` (refresh layers) and `c` (run missing chunks) in the modal. `/review layers` prints the same lines.
